title: Milvus vs LanceDB: Lance Format, Scale, Capabilities
description: Milvus vs LanceDB: Lance vs LanceDB explained, how Milvus searches Lance datasets in place, Milvus Lite vs embedded LanceDB, and where distributed compute matters.

h1: Milvus vs LanceDB: format, embedded library, or distributed database?
intro: Milvus vs LanceDB is really a comparison of layers: Lance is an open columnar format, LanceDB is the embedded database built over it, and Milvus is a distributed vector database that can serve Lance datasets in place or store data itself. LanceDB OSS runs inside one application process; Milvus runs as a service with storage-compute separation, replicas and multi-writer ingest. Keep Lance as your source of truth either way; choose LanceDB when one process owns the data, and Milvus when many services, writers or tenants share it.

sections.h2: Lance vs LanceDB: what is the difference?
paragraphs: Lance is an open, Arrow-native lakehouse format for multimodal AI (Apache-2.0, lance-format/lance). It is three specs in one: a file format whose column pages are laid out for fast random access, a table format that manages fragments, manifests, deletions, schema evolution and ACID commits as immutable versions, and index formats that make vector, full-text and scalar indexes first-class, versioned table objects.

LanceDB is the database built on top of Lance. LanceDB OSS is an embedded retrieval library with Python, TypeScript and Rust SDKs that organizes Lance datasets into named tables and runs search inside your process; LanceDB Cloud and Enterprise are the company's hosted and BYOC services that add always-on query nodes, plan executors and indexers over the same tables. Lance format vs Parquet is a storage question; LanceDB vs Milvus is a serving question.

sections.h2: Can Milvus use Lance as a storage format too?
paragraphs: Yes. A Milvus external collection (Milvus 3.0+) points external_source at a Lance dataset directory with format lance-table, maps each field to a source column with external_field, and then indexes and serves the data in place. There is no import and no second copy: the rows stay in Lance, read-only, and Milvus stores only the schema mapping, manifests, indexes and caches.
Your Lance datasets stay the source of truth; Milvus adds the serving layer. Spark, Ray or pylance keep writing fragments, and the same files remain readable by LanceDB, DuckDB and training jobs.
bullets: Enable Storage V3 (common.storage.useLoonFFI: true), create the schema with external_source and external_spec, then refresh, index, load and search.
Milvus builds its own HNSW, IVF or DiskANN index in Milvus storage and never writes into the dataset, so Lance's native indexes and versions are untouched.
Refresh is explicit, asynchronous and incremental: new fragments are picked up, unchanged data keeps its segments and indexes, and queries serve the previous state until it completes.
External fields can feed Functions, so BM25 sparse vectors or text embeddings are generated in Milvus without writing a column back to the table.
The same mechanism reads Apache Iceberg tables (format iceberg-table with a snapshot_id), Parquet and Vortex; see vector search on the data lake.

sections.h2: Milvus and LanceDB: from embedded retrieval to distributed serving
paragraphs: For the embedded case, Milvus Lite is a pip install (pymilvus) that runs in-process and keeps data in a local file: MilvusClient("./milvus_demo.db"). It targets notebooks, laptops, edge devices and prototypes, and the same MilvusClient API moves unchanged to Standalone, Distributed and Zilliz Cloud. That is the LanceDB OSS shape: zero services, one process, local storage.

The core difference is what happens past one process. Milvus is a distributed system with storage-compute separation: stateless proxies, streaming nodes for writes and the WAL, query nodes for search, and data nodes for compaction and index build, all over shared object storage. Multiple clients write at once, replicas raise throughput and absorb failures, a query fans out across query nodes, and tiered storage keeps hot data in memory and local disk while the rest stays in object storage. LanceDB OSS is bound to its host process; its docs put OSS at millions of vectors on a single node and recommend LanceDB Enterprise, which adds its own query nodes, plan executors, indexers and a control plane, for hundreds of millions and beyond.

sections.h2: LanceDB vs Milvus features: what each does that the other does not
paragraphs: LanceDB's edge is the data layer: because the table is Lance, the same files flow through Arrow, pandas, Polars, DuckDB and PyTorch, every write is a time-travelable version, and images or audio sit next to their embeddings as blobs. Milvus's edge is the serving layer: server-side hybrid search with BM25, fused by RRF, weighted, decay or model rankers and composed with Function Chain; partition-key multi-tenancy for millions of tenants; RBAC; a broad index catalog including GPU, DiskANN and RaBitQ; streaming ingest that is searchable on write under a chosen consistency level; and external collections over Lance and Iceberg.

sections.h2: When is LanceDB the better choice?
paragraphs: What is LanceDB good at? Removing a tier. For a single process that owns its data, LanceDB OSS gives you search, full-text and versioned storage from a library and a directory. If that process later needs to share the data with other services, the Lance files are already the kind of thing Milvus serves.
bullets: A single-process app, notebook, CLI or edge function that wants search with no server.
Local-first development where the dataset fits one machine and ships with the code.
Lance-native pipelines: PyTorch, Ray or Spark jobs that train on and query the same versioned table.
Multimodal datasets where images, audio and embeddings belong in one table with time travel.
Teams that want Arrow, DuckDB and Polars on the same files as their vector search.

sections.h2: Which AI companies and enterprises run Milvus in production?
paragraphs: Milvus and Zilliz Cloud (managed Milvus) run in AI-native companies and large enterprises alike. The milvus.io adopter wall includes Salesforce, Walmart, NVIDIA, eBay, IBM, Cisco, Roblox, and Reddit, alongside Exa.ai, OpenEvidence, Read.ai, Notta.ai, Plaud, and Filevine. Published results:
bullets: OpenEvidence: under 10 ms search latency and 4,000 QPS at peak on Zilliz Cloud.
Plaud: 10B+ vector chunks per region with under 200 ms average recall latency.
Exa: neural search latency cut from seconds to under 200 ms with hybrid search.
Airtable: self-hosts Milvus on Kubernetes with the Milvus Operator for semantic search.

faqs: What is the difference between Lance and LanceDB?

Lance is the open columnar format: files, versioned tables of fragments, and native vector, full-text and scalar indexes, all Arrow-native. LanceDB is the database built on it: an embedded OSS library that queries Lance tables in-process, plus LanceDB Cloud and Enterprise services. Milvus reads Lance too.

Yes. A Milvus 3.0+ external collection points external_source at the Lance dataset directory with format lance-table, maps columns with external_field, then refreshes, indexes and serves it. Rows stay in Lance, read-only, with no second copy; Storage V3 (common.storage.useLoonFFI) must be enabled.

In shape, yes: Milvus Lite is pip-installed, runs in your Python process and stores data in a local file, like LanceDB OSS. It is meant for prototypes and edge use with a FLAT index; the same MilvusClient code then runs on Milvus Standalone, Distributed or Zilliz Cloud.
Is LanceDB production-ready, and how far does it scale?

LanceDB's docs say OSS comfortably handles millions of vectors on a single node, with bounded commit retries under many concurrent writers, and recommend LanceDB Enterprise for hundreds of millions and beyond. Milvus Distributed is documented for tens of billions of vectors with replicas and multi-writer ingest.
Can LanceDB and Milvus share the same Lance data?

Yes. Milvus never writes into the dataset: it keeps its own indexes in Milvus storage, so LanceDB, DuckDB, Spark and training jobs keep reading and writing the same Lance files while Milvus serves online search over them.
What is the difference between Milvus and Zilliz Cloud?

Zilliz Cloud is fully managed Milvus from the team that created it, with the same client APIs, so code written against Milvus Lite or Standalone moves there without a rewrite. It also offers external collections over Lance, Iceberg, Parquet and Vortex.External collections are currently in Public Preview and supported only in on-demand compute databases.
